prompt: `vnet-shop-prod` is moved from `rg-shop-prod` to `rg-shop-prod-network` in the same subscription. What changes?
hint: Read the id before and after.

choices.text: Its region, to the destination group's region
choices.why: A move never changes the region. The group's own location is only where its record lives.

choices.text: Nothing, as long as both groups are in one subscription
choices.why: Even inside one subscription the group is part of the id, so the id changes.

choices.text: Its address space, which is renumbered on arrival
choices.why: Nothing about the network itself changes. Its users notice nothing.

choices.text: Its resource id
choices.why: Right. The group in the path is rewritten, and so is everything that stored the old path.

prompt: While a move from `rg-shop-prod` to `rg-shop-prod-network` runs, a release pipeline tries to deploy a web app into `rg-shop-prod`. What happens to the release?
hint: Both groups are in the same state during a move.

choices.text: It is refused: both groups are locked
choices.why: Right. Existing resources keep working; nothing in either group can be created or changed.

choices.text: It is queued and runs when the move finishes
choices.why: Nothing queues it. The request is refused, and the pipeline has to try again.

choices.text: It succeeds, since the web app is not being moved
choices.why: The lock is on the whole group, not only on the resources being moved.

choices.text: It lands in `rg-shop-prod-network` instead
choices.why: A deployment goes where it is aimed or nowhere.

prompt: bia had the Contributor role assigned directly on `vnet-shop-prod`. The network moves to another resource group. What happens to her assignment?
hint: Does an assignment on the resource travel with it?

choices.text: It moves with the network
choices.why: Assignments on the resource are left behind; that is the documented behaviour.

choices.text: It stays behind, orphaned
choices.why: Right. Azure removes the orphan eventually; the new one is yours to create.

choices.text: It is converted into an assignment on the new group
choices.why: Nothing converts it, and a group-wide grant would be a much wider permission.

choices.text: The move is refused until the assignment is removed
choices.why: The move goes ahead; Microsoft only recommends removing it first.

prompt: The shop moves `shop-staging` from `mg-shop-nonprod` to `mg-shop-prod`. Which statement is true the second it finishes?
hint: A subscription's id does not mention its management group.

choices.text: Every resource id in `shop-staging` has changed
choices.why: Resource ids name the subscription, never its management group.

choices.text: The resources in it are locked until the move ends
choices.why: Nothing is locked when a subscription changes branch.

choices.text: Its resources now inherit production's policies
choices.why: Right. Nothing is renamed and nothing moves; the rules that apply change at once.

choices.text: Staging's resources are moved into production's region
choices.why: A management group has no region, and nothing is relocated.

prompt: A move between resource groups changes a resource's id and never its ___.
hint: Azure Resource Mover exists for changing this.

prompt: Where does `moves.py` get its answers from?
hint: Look at `URL`.

choices.text: From a page of Microsoft's documentation
choices.why: Right. The same table the documentation shows, read as Markdown.

choices.text: From a list built into the Azure CLI
choices.why: The CLI carries no such list.

choices.text: From Resource Manager, which it asks for each type
choices.why: It never talks to Azure. It would be refused here if it did.

choices.text: From a file the student writes by hand
choices.why: It downloads the table every time it runs.

prompt: `moves.py` reported `Microsoft.Network/loadBalancers` as `depends` for subscriptions. What did the table's cell say?
hint: A cell can carry both words.

choices.text: Nothing: load balancers are missing from the table
choices.why: A missing type answers `?`, not `depends`.

choices.text: Yes for the Basic SKU and No for the Standard
choices.why: Right. Both words in one cell is what the program calls `depends`.

choices.text: No, with a link to the networking guidance
choices.why: A No with a link is still only a No once the link is stripped.

choices.text: That it depends on the region of the subscription
choices.why: Region is not part of the rule; the version of the product is.

prompt: The shop wants its NAT gateway in `rg-shop-prod-network` instead of `rg-shop-prod`. By the table, what is the way?
hint: The NAT gateway's row says No twice.

choices.text: Move it with `az resource move`, since a move inside one subscription always works
choices.why: The table's first column is exactly the move inside a subscription, and it says No.

choices.text: Move the subnet it is attached to, and it follows
choices.why: It is not a child of the subnet, and a subnet does not move alone either.

choices.text: Ask Microsoft support to move it
choices.why: Support cannot move a type the platform does not move.

choices.text: Create a new one there and delete the old
choices.why: Right. A type that cannot move is recreated, with a short change of outbound addresses.

prompt: The table says Yes for moving `publicIPAddresses` between subscriptions. A VM uses a Standard public IP. Can the shop move the VM and its IP to `shop-shared`?
hint: What does the page the row links to add?

choices.text: Yes: the table's Yes covers it
choices.why: The cell is the start of the answer. The networking guidance adds the exception.

choices.text: Yes, provided both are in one resource group
choices.why: That is necessary for any move across subscriptions, and not enough here.

choices.text: No: the linked guidance excludes that case
choices.why: Right. A Yes in the table sends you to read the linked page.

choices.text: Only after upgrading the IP from Basic to Standard
choices.why: Standard is the version that cannot cross; upgrading goes the wrong way.

prompt: On the day the lesson read it, how many resource types did Microsoft's move table list?
hint: The first line `moves.py` printed.

prompt: Why does `moves.py` lower-case the type names it stores and looks up?
hint: Lesson 2 typed an id carelessly.

choices.text: Because Azure ignores case in type names
choices.why: Right. `virtualNetworks` and `virtualnetworks` are one type, so the lookup treats them as one.

choices.text: To make the output shorter
choices.why: Case does not change length, and the output prints the name as typed.

choices.text: Because the table spells every type in capitals
choices.why: The table spells them in lower case, and people type them otherwise.

choices.text: Because Python dictionaries refuse capital letters
choices.why: Dictionaries take any string as a key.

prompt: What does `validateMoveResources` do?
hint: It is the check before the move.

choices.text: It moves the resources and rolls back if anything fails
choices.why: It moves nothing at all.

choices.text: It lists the types the subscription may hold
choices.why: That is the provider registration, a different question.

choices.text: It says whether the move would succeed
choices.why: Right. The portal runs it before every move.

choices.text: It locks the two groups in advance
choices.why: The lock comes with the move itself.

prompt: A network is moved into `shop-shared`, which has never held a network. The move fails with *the subscription isn't registered for a resource type*. What fixes it?
hint: Creating a resource does it on the way; a move does not.

choices.text: Moving the network to a new resource group first
choices.why: The group is not the problem; the destination subscription is.

choices.text: Raising the subscription's quota for networks
choices.why: A quota failure says so; this message is about registration.

choices.text: Signing in to the destination tenant instead
choices.why: Both subscriptions trust the same tenant, or the move would have failed earlier.

choices.text: Registering the provider there
choices.why: Right. `az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Network` in `shop-shared`: the destination has to be registered before it can hold the provider's resources.

prompt: Put the steps of moving a VM whose network sits in another resource group to another subscription in order.
hint: Dependencies have to share a group before they cross.
items: check the types against the move table
move the network into the VM's group, inside the source subscription
move the whole group's worth to the destination in one request
split them into groups again at the destination
trap: The validation comes after the gathering: it checks the move you are about to make, with everything already in one group.

prompt: `vnet-shop-prod` is peered with the hub. What does the networking guidance require before it moves?
hint: Lesson 20's subject has to be undone.

choices.text: Nothing: peerings move with the network as children
choices.why: The guidance says the peering has to be removed first.

choices.text: Remove the peering, move, then make it again
choices.why: Right. The two networks are disconnected for the duration.

choices.text: Moving the hub network in the same request
choices.why: The hub stays; it is the peering that has to go.

choices.text: Converting the peering into a VPN connection
choices.why: No such conversion is part of a move.

prompt: Which of these make a move fail or be refused, by Microsoft's checklist? Choose all that apply.
hint: Read the table of the section as a list of failures.

choices.text: A read-only lock on the destination group
choices.why: Right. A lock on either group or subscription refuses it.

choices.text: The two subscriptions trusting different tenants
choices.why: Right. That is a change of directory, not a move.

choices.text: The source and destination groups being in different regions
choices.why: A group's location is only its record's; it does not stop a move.

choices.text: No quota left in the destination
choices.why: Right. What arrives counts against the destination's limits.

choices.text: A resource with tags
choices.why: Tags travel with a resource and stop nothing.

prompt: A startup's subscription was opened with the founder's personal account, and now must join the company's tenant. Which warning from the lesson applies?
hint: This is a change of directory, not a move.

choices.text: Every resource id will change and has to be updated
choices.why: The subscription keeps its id; what is lost is everything tied to the old tenant.

choices.text: The resources have to be moved to one group first
choices.why: That is the rule for moving resources across subscriptions, not for changing a subscription's tenant.

choices.text: The subscription must first be moved to the root management group
choices.why: Management groups belong to a tenant and play no part in changing it.

choices.text: Role assignments and managed identities do not survive it
choices.why: Right. They belonged to the old tenant, and have to be made again in the new one.

prompt: Before a destination subscription can hold networks, it has to be ___ for the `Microsoft.Network` namespace.
hint: `az provider ...`

prompt: Which of these moves keeps every resource id exactly as it was?
hint: What does an id name, and what does it not?

choices.text: A network to another resource group
choices.why: The group is in the id, so the id changes.

choices.text: A subscription to another management group
choices.why: Right. Ids never mention a management group.

choices.text: A VM and its dependencies to another subscription
choices.why: The subscription is in the id too.

choices.text: A key vault to a group in another region
choices.why: The vault's region does not change, but its group does, and the group is in the id.

prompt: Match each of the shop's resource types to what the move table said about it on the day of recording.
hint: Two say No twice; one differs between the columns.

pairs.right: moves to another group and another subscription
depends on the SKU across subscriptions

prompt: A colleague plans to move every resource of `rg-shop-prod` to a group in `southcentralus` "so that it fails over to Texas". What is wrong with the plan?
hint: What does a group's location decide, and what does a move change?

choices.text: A move never changes where a resource runs
choices.why: Right. The resources stay in São Paulo; only their group's name in the id changes.

choices.text: Groups in Texas cannot hold resources from Brazil
choices.why: They can: a group's resources may be in any region.

choices.text: Moving to a paired region needs Microsoft's approval
choices.why: No approval exists, because no relocation happens.

choices.text: The firewall and NAT gateway would be left in São Paulo
choices.why: True of those two types, but it is not why the plan fails: nothing would go to Texas.
